reviewedFrom: B09.2 definition of done (advisor-plans/013): >1,000 records and repeated cursor ties exactly once; interruption/resume and concurrent workers without skips or duplicates; work scales with selected sources, not the ledger.

first-run-ties-idle-and-one-change.derivation: 1,200 approved bills of 1,000.00, all sharing one updated_at an hour old, so the runs measure a settled ledger rather than the 5-minute late-commit window. The first run posts 1,200 entries, one per bill, with 1,200 receipts and AP of 1,200,000.00. An idle run then reads only configuration (projects, accounts, policies, cursors: at most 200 rows) and calls neither the projection nor the receipt RPC. Re-coding one bill makes exactly one projection call and reads at most 300 rows, not the 1,200-bill ledger or its 1,200 job-cost lines.

interrupted-run-resumes.derivation: A worker process running the ordinary 10-minute pass over 1,200 new bills is killed with SIGKILL once 300 receipts exist. One ordinary run afterwards completes the other bills: 1,200 posted entries for 1,200 distinct bills, 1,200 receipts, AP 1,200,000.00.

concurrent-workers.derivation: Three ordinary runs start at once over the same 1,200 new bills (each may also see the others' work), followed by one more ordinary run. Every bill has exactly one posted entry and one receipt; AP 1,200,000.00.

late-commit.derivation: Two posted bills. A transaction begins re-dating the first to July 11 and holds for 6 seconds, so its updated_at is its start time. Meanwhile the second is re-dated to July 12 through the product and a run posts it, advancing the cursor past the first's timestamp. After the first commits, the next ordinary run must still re-post it on July 11.

nightly-pass.derivation: After the 1,200 bills post, a full pass with nothing changed makes no projection or receipt calls. The project then moves into a new division. Under the reporting-tag policy (tags stay as posted, decided 2026-10-06 with B07), neither the ordinary run nor the nightly pass re-posts any bill, and the posted bills keep no division. A bill approved afterwards on the same project posts with the North division on its lines. Re-coding one of the posted bills afterwards is a real revision: it re-posts with the North division.

time-budget.derivation: A company with one approved bill. A cron pass whose deadline has already passed reaches no company: each gets an open projection_failed finding on the company itself, nothing posts, and the July close is held by the open finding. The next pass, with a 10-minute budget over every company on the stack, reaches it, posts the bill and resolves the finding.

failed-source-retries.derivation: A bill whose posting the database refuses (a temporary trigger stands in for a transient failure) opens a projection_failed finding and posts nothing. A newer bill then posts, moving the bills cursor past the failed one. The refusal is removed without touching the bill; the next ordinary run reads the failed bill by its open finding, posts it on July 10 and resolves the finding.

close-review-reads.derivation: Two companies, identical except for volume: 120 and 1,200 posted July bills. The July close checklist runs for each and its tie-outs pass at both sizes (AP ties to the AP subledger, GL job cost ties to the job-cost subledger). The larger review reads no journal lines, journal entries or job-cost lines (ledger totals, job cost, clearing positions and WIP activity are summed in the database), reads each of its 1,200 payable bills exactly once (the AP and AP-retainage subledger it proves), and otherwise reads at most 200 more rows than the smaller one.

narrowed-proof.derivation: 1,200 posted bills, then damage written straight to the database: bill A's journal amounts raised by one cent per side; a copy of bill B's journal posted with no fact behind it; bill D re-dated to July 20 without its updated_at moving. Bill C is then approved through the product and never projected. The full rebuild drill sees A (journal_divergence) and B (unexpected_journal) and cannot see C or D. The narrowed proof over every bill finds the same two plus C (missing_fact) and D (stale_fact). Over ten chosen bills including A it finds only A, checks ten sources and reads at most 300 rows. Over everything changed since the damage it finds C, and B's stray journal (inserted now); A and D bypassed their timestamps, which is what the weekly full drill is for.
